subject: general
question:
**Change the following from active to passive:**

We are going to start the project soon.

options.text: The project is going to be started soon.
The project was going to be started soon.
The project is being going to be started soon.
The project has been going to be started soon.

solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. The project is going to be started soon .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided is in the **active voice**, where the subject "We" is performing the action.
 
• To change it to the **passive voice**, the focus shifts to the object "the project," and the action is expressed as being done to the object.
 
• The correct passive construction follows the structure: **Object + form of 'be' + past participle**.
 
• In this case, the verb "start" becomes "is going to be started."

Correct sentence: *The project is going to be started soon*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action (e.g., "We are going to start the project").
 
• **Passive Voice:** The action is performed on the object (e.g., "The project is going to be started").
 
• In passive voice, the auxiliary verb changes according to the tense in the active voice.
